full_judgment:
2. The petitioners filed the application under Article 102, of the Constitution stating, inter alia. That petitioners have taken loan of Taka 1,30,000/- from the respondent No. 2 on 28-11-1984 for construction of 10 storied building on plot No. 60, Gulshan Avenue hereinafter called the case property. Before completion of the building the respondent No.2 put pressure to liquidate the loan money. The petitioners paid back part of the amount of the loan money. The respondent No.2 then filed Title Suit No. 22 of 1991 in the Court of respondent No.1 for realisation of money and obtained a decree on 8-10-1992 in the suit for realisation of money by selling the mortgaged property. The decree was put into execution in Title Execution Case No. 38 of 1994 before the respondent No.1, who on 17-6-1998 issued a sale proclamation for sale of the case property under Order XXI rule 66 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The Executing Court by the impugned order dated 10-8-1998 most illegally ordered for deposit of Taka 1,00,000/- (Taka one lac) only as security money by the participants at the bid. The respondent No. 2 purchased the case property through bid in collusion with the office staffs of the Court at a low price. 

 7. The decision in the case of Sultana Jute Mills Ltd vs Agrani Bank reported in 46 DLR (AD) 174 though was on the question of maintainability of the revisional jurisdiction against an order passed while trying the suit under the Artha Rin Adalat Ain but in the case of Islami Bank Bangladesh vs Md Shafiuddin reported in 52 DLR (AD) 76 it has been held that under section 5(4) of the Altha Rin Adalat it is a civil Court having all the powers and jurisdiction under the Civil Procedure Code, 1908, subject to the provision of the Ain. In the instant case the impugned order has been passed in the execution proceeding and the petitioner could avail the provision of Order XXI rule 90 of the Code of Civil Procedure in setting aside the auction sale on ground of material irregularity and fraud alleged by any of the party to the execution proceeding arising out of judgment and decree passed under the Ain as the same could have been adequately dealt with under the said provision and in the facts and circumstances of the instant case the writ jurisdiction is not maintainable for deciding the question of fraud and material irregularity in publishing and conducting the sale which are essentially a question of fact to be determined on evidence and could not be conveniently dealt with in writ jurisdiction. Reference in this regard may be made in the case of Sardar Jan-e-Alam vs Arab Bangladesh Bank Lid and others reported in 4 BLC (AD) 178.
